newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-David Jones to review some stores.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-David Jones to review some stores.

text.p: Upmarket retailer David Jones Ltd said on Wednesday that it would review operations at about five or six of its department stores which were underperforming.

Chairman Richard Warburton said about one-third of David Jones stores were performing very well, another third were making a profit, but could be improved, while the final third were underperforming and not returning any shareholder value.
Warburton said five or six of these underperforming stores would be reviewed.

"You have got a final third that's just not producing shareholder value. They are not necessarily losing money but they are not increasing shareholder value," Warburton told reporters. He said David Jones had about 30 stores.
"Out of that third a half, I believe, with a bit of hard work and creative juices could take them above the line, the other half we have to look at very, very closely," Warburton said.
"So you can see we have about five or six stores to look at, that does not necessarily mean closure. It may mean you have to look at different things to do with those stores," he said.
"What we have said if you can't close them, you have got to find creative ways of using utilising them," Warburton said.
David Jones spent about A$24.4 million on new stores, store refurbishment and informational technology in the 1996/97 first half, down from A$36.2 million a year earlier.
It said there was A$8.0 million in costs with the operation of the three new stores Tuggerah, New South Wales, Glen Waverley, Victoria, and Robina, in Queensland.
David Jones also plans to open new stores in New Zealand and Western Australia.
David Jones earlier reported a 50 percent fall in first half net profit for the 26 weeks to January 25, 1997 to A$22.3 million from A$44.6 million.

Finance director Robert Wright told reporters David Jones planned A$50 million in capital expenditure in the 1996/97 year. At 12.45 p.m. (0145 GMT), David Jones shares were three cents lower at A$1.71.
